C

The energy dissipated is equal to the work done by the braking force, which by the work-energy theorem equals the change in the car's kinetic energy. The work done is W = ∫ F dx = m ∫ a dx. The integral ∫ a dx is the area under the acceleration-distance graph from d=0 to d=40 m. This area is calculated to be -80 m²/s². The work done is W = 1500 kg × (-80 m²/s²) = -120 kJ. The energy dissipated is the magnitude of this work, 120 kJ.
